page: Amazon Web Services r5.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by custom Intel Xeon Platinum 8175M processors operating at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this bare-metal offering provides direct access to 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 768.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB RAM per physical core ratio. The instance includes a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core throughput and memory performance. The instance achieved a strong multi-core score of 81870.14 in stress-ng and a PassMark CPU score of 57080.9, complemented by high-bandwidth memory read speeds reaching 222.69 GB/sec on large uncached blocks. In-memory processing benchmarks show notable throughput, including 74.16 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and high ratings in database operations. Conversely, single-thread metrics such as Geekbench single-core (1207.0) and stress-ng single-core (1450.99) remain within average performance ranges.

Because the r5.metal instance lacks local NVMe storage and GPUs, persistent data pipelines require network-attached storage architectures, and text generation tasks on large language models perform poorly compared to accelerated options. With 768 GB of memory on dedicated hardware without hypervisor overhead, it offers strong resource density for memory-bound applications. The instance is suited for large enterprise in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, Redis clusters, and batch compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r5.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server equipped with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8175M processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture without hypervisor virtualization overhead, the system delivers direct hardware access combined with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory across an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network bandwidth operates at a baseline of 25 Gbps, with zero local storage bundled and no integrated GPUs. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show strong parallel computing capacity and memory throughput, evidenced by 74.16 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a 57080.9 PassMark CPU score, though single-core execution remains average. The hardware profile is optimal for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, distributed analytics, and large build jobs.
